newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index options brisk, puts focus.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index options brisk, puts focus.

text.p: Another whipsaw in U.S. stocks kept index options activity brisk and volatility up, traders said Monday.
By 1415 CST/2015 GMT, most market indices had erased solid intraday advances, with some slipping into negative ground.
The S&P 100 index, on which most index options are traded, was off about a point at 729 after being up nearly seven intraday.
The S&P 500 index was down three at 745 after rising more than five to 753.30.
Index put options continued to see most oder flow, even as the market rallied, suggesting to some traders that investors were seeking protection after last Friday's market rally.
"It's another rock and roll day," Michael Schwartz at Oppenheimer said of the market's activity.
At 1400 CST/2000 GMT, OEX put volume outpaced call volume by 51,697 to 44,865. SPX put volume on the CBOE topped call volume by 31,440 to 24,927.
Trading in SPX options was led by the January 725 and 730 puts, which traded roughly 8,770 and 8,360 contracts, respectively.
Those two puts traded in fairly wide ranges, with the 725 put bouncing between 5-1/8, a contract low, and 8-5/8. The 730 put traded between a new contract low of 6-1/2 and 10-7/8.
The most active OEX call was the January 735, which traded about 7,540 contracts at prices ranging from 6-5/8 to 11-1/2.
Despite the market's fluctuations, traders said most of the options remained expensive.
One trader noted that in late trading, with the OEX fluctuating around 730, the at-the-money January 730 calls were still priced at 10-3/4 and the January 730 puts were trading at nine.
In a report, analyst Jerry Hegarty at Thomson Financial Services said he expects OEX put buying to continue to outpace OEX call buying, which is a bullish indication.
He noted that last Friday, put buying topped call buying by a five-to-four ratio.

In SPX options trading at the Chicago Board Options Exchange, put option volume also led call volume, but the biggest concentrations were seen in two calls, the January 750 and January 760, which traded 5,815 and 5,560 contracts, respectively.
The most active SPX put was the January 710 put, which traded roughly 5,450 contracts. The option was up 3/16 at 1-5/8, having traded between 1-1/6, a new contract low, and two.
The January 710 call traded about 4,015 contracts. It was up 7/8 at 44-1/2.
